html:
SMTO-UI-0059 — Only an administrator can do this

GUID: ae05805b-4ac5-5cd2-a96b-25570c7f28b3
Slug: admin-required
Domain: UI · Subsystem: authentication

What happened

  • Your account is a regular user account. This action changes how SMTO is set up for everyone, so only an administrator can do it. SMTO didn't change anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Write down what you were trying to do, such as which page you opened or which setting you wanted to change. The administrator needs to know exactly which change you need.
  2. Ask your SMTO administrator to make the change from their own account. Administrator accounts may change server-wide setup; regular accounts are blocked from it on purpose.
  3. If your job needs you to manage SMTO, ask an existing administrator to change your Role to Admin on the Users page. What you're allowed to do comes from the role on your account, so changing the role is the lasting fix.

What success looks like

  • The administrator confirms the change is done, or the page opens for you after your role is changed (sign out and back in if it still refuses).

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to your administrator together with the name of the page you were using. Never include your password or browser cookies.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The portal middleware returned admin_required (403) because a non-admin session requested an installation-level route (Settings, Users, console, inference, server, update, Gateway management, model routing and similar) or the portal is running admin-only.

What this means

  • Your account cannot perform this installation-level action. This reports access to the current request, not the outcome of previous operations.

Why this can happen

  • Your account cannot perform this installation-level action.

How to diagnose it

  • The administrator completes the requested action and checks its result.

How to fix it

  • This is a role check in PortalAuthMiddleware (smto_runtime.principal.admin_route), not a fault. Have an administrator perform the action from their own account, or, if this user should have installation authority, set the account's Role to Admin on the Users page (/user).
  • Ask an administrator to carry out this action from their own workspace. Share the error reference and the feature you were using.

Retry and execution caution

  • The administrator completes the requested action and checks its result.

How to verify the fix

  • The administrator completes the requested action and checks its result.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained task data or repeat an operation with an unknown outcome.

Technical notes

  • Authentication guidance never changes account permissions or replays task work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
